name: חישוב מכפלה וקטורית של שני וקטורים (באנגלית)

functions.name: texp
functions.body: if numberp(x) and x<0 then concat("\\left(",tex1(x),"\\right)") else tex1(x)

functions.name: texsumf
functions.body: block([L:first(args(e))], concat(tex1(first(L)), apply(sconcat, map(lambda([t], concat("+",texp(t))), rest(L)))))

functions.name: texnsum
functions.body: block([L:first(args(e))], concat(tex1(first(L)), apply(sconcat, map(lambda([t], if numberp(t) and t<0 then concat("-",tex1(-t)) else concat("+",tex1(t))), rest(L)))))

questiontext:
Calculate the vector product \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v}\) where \(\underline{u}\) has components {{CT:0}} and \(\underline{v}\) has components {{CT:1}}.

\(\underline{u}\times\underline{v} =\) [[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]

How to enter: each entry in its own box: a number, a fraction (e.g. 1/2) or an expression (e.g. sqrt(2)).
generalfeedback:
Outline: The vector product of \(\underline{u}=(u_1,u_2,u_3)\) and \(\underline{v}=(v_1,v_2,v_3)\) is computed component by component from the formula \(\underline{u}\times\underline{v}=(u_2v_3-u_3v_2,\ u_3v_1-u_1v_3,\ u_1v_2-u_2v_1)\), which is the expansion of the determinant with \(\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j},\mathbf{k}\) in its first row.
Step 1 — The determinant
Write the components of the two vectors under the unit vectors and expand along the first row:

\[ \underline{u}\times\underline{v}=\det\begin{pmatrix} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ {{CT:2}} & {{CT:3}} & {{CT:4}} \\ {{CT:5}} & {{CT:6}} & {{CT:7}} \end{pmatrix} \]

Step 2 — The components
Here \(u_1,u_2,u_3\) are the components of \(\underline{u}\) and \(v_1,v_2,v_3\) those of \(\underline{v}\):

\[ \begin{aligned} (\underline{u}\times\underline{v})_1 &= u_2v_3-u_3v_2 = {{CT:8}}-{{CT:9}} = {{CT:10}} = {{CT:11}} \\ (\underline{u}\times\underline{v})_2 &= u_3v_1-u_1v_3 = {{CT:12}}-{{CT:13}} = {{CT:14}} = {{CT:15}} \\ (\underline{u}\times\underline{v})_3 &= u_1v_2-u_2v_1 = {{CT:16}}-{{CT:17}} = {{CT:18}} = {{CT:19}} \end{aligned} \]

Hence

\[ \underline{u}\times\underline{v}={{CT:20}} \]
